problem.headline: Your Studio's Knowledge Shouldn't Be Scattered.
problem.lead: Game studios accumulate years of technical decisions across source repositories, wikis, design documents, engine references, and different project branches. Generic AI coding tools only see isolated code snippets—leaving developers to hunt manually for the engineering context behind every system.

painPoints.title: Where systems are actually implemented
painPoints.detail: Gameplay mechanics rarely live in one file. Tracing where damage, progression, inventory, or physics logic executes across client and server scripts burns senior engineering hours.

painPoints.title: Which components depend on them
painPoints.detail: Hidden coupling across modules, components, remote events, and engine subsystems turns routine feature work into risky trial-and-error.

painPoints.title: Which documents explain the design intent
painPoints.detail: Design specs, onboarding notes, and architecture decisions drift away from code in separate folders, wikis, and historical discussions.

painPoints.title: Which engine references apply to your version
painPoints.detail: Roblox Studio APIs and Unreal Engine C++ headers evolve continuously. Developers need references tied to the engine version their studio actually ships on.

painPoints.title: What could be affected by a change
painPoints.detail: Without connected code-and-doc context, engineers struggle to inspect blast radius, edge cases, and upstream assumptions before modifying production systems.

architecture.eyebrow: The Solution · Powered by Project Forge
architecture.headline: One Connected View of Your Engineering Knowledge.
architecture.lead: Project Forge indexes your approved source files, technical documentation, and design notes into an isolated retrieval layer (with scoped engine reference packs in development)—so developers can investigate their project through MCP-compatible AI tools and inspect every answer against real project evidence.
architecture.boundaryNote: The workflow below represents the intended Studio Intelligence Hub service architecture delivered through scoped four-week managed pilots. Pilot scope is currently in testing on FDS's own Roblox and Unreal projects—no Hub runtime capability is claimed as tested and certified until forge-hub runtime tests pass. Exact ingestion sources and tool hooks are agreed during your Week 1 technical assessment.

securityControls.title: Read-Only Project Access
securityControls.detail: The Hub has no write tools and never writes into your repository. Pilots also run it against a read-only copy of your approved branches, enforced by the operating system, so connected AI tools cannot change it either.

securityControls.title: Customer-Controlled Environment
securityControls.detail: Deployment boundaries are agreed before kickoff so your studio stays in control of where project context lives and who can query it.

securityControls.title: Customer-Owned API Keys
securityControls.detail: Your studio supplies and controls its own AI provider API keys and pays its chosen AI provider directly. FDS does not route consumer subscriptions or mark up token bills.

securityControls.title: No Repository Modifications
securityControls.detail: Cannot modify your repository — read-only by design.

securityControls.title: Isolated Project Data
securityControls.detail: Each pilot gets its own install, index, and report folders, kept separate from your source and from every other studio.

securityControls.title: No Training Without Written Permission
securityControls.detail: FDS never uses your studio's code, documents, or questions to train FDS models without your explicit written permission. Whether your AI provider may use conversations for training is controlled by your provider account settings, which we review with you before the pilot.

securityControls.title: Agreed Data-Deletion Steps
securityControls.detail: Retention boundaries and data-deletion steps are agreed in writing at pilot kickoff and carried out on request or at pilot closeout.

faqs.q: Is the Studio Intelligence Hub a self-serve SaaS product I can sign up for today?
faqs.a: No. FDS Studio Intelligence Hub is delivered as a managed, scoped four-week pilot service—not a finished, generally available SaaS platform. Pilot capabilities are currently in testing on FDS's own Roblox and Unreal projects, and every engagement begins with a technical assessment call to confirm whether your repository layout, engine, and documentation fit current pilot scope.

faqs.q: Does the Unreal Engine pilot index Blueprints?
faqs.a: No—not yet. Our Unreal Engine pilot scope covers C++ source code, headers, module structure, technical documentation, and design specs (scoped engine reference packs are in development). Blueprint visual graph indexing has not been implemented yet, so we do not advertise or promise Blueprint understanding.

faqs.q: Do we have to install Jaspilite to use the Studio Intelligence Hub?
faqs.a: No. Jaspilite is not a prerequisite for the Studio Intelligence Hub. Project Forge is designed to connect into existing external MCP-compatible development tools your engineers already use.

faqs.q: How do AI models and API billing work during the pilot?
faqs.a: Your studio uses its own AI provider API keys and pays your chosen AI provider directly under your provider's own terms. FDS does not bundle unlimited AI inference, does not route consumer subscriptions through our software, and does not add opaque token markups.

Pilot pricing depends on your engine, codebase scope, and project configuration, and is discussed clearly during your initial pilot assessment call before any commitment. The first five Founding Studios receive 50% off the applicable pilot fee in exchange for structured feedback.

faqs.q: How does FDS protect our unannounced game code and design documents?
faqs.a: The Hub cannot modify your repository — it is read-only by design. Pilots use isolated per-project data and customer-owned API keys; data-deletion steps are agreed in writing at kickoff, and FDS never trains FDS models on your data without explicit written permission. We also stay honest about governance: FDS does not claim SOC 2, ISO 27001, or third-party enterprise compliance certifications.

faqs.q: Does the Hub promise 100% accurate AI answers?
faqs.a: No AI system can promise 100% accuracy. The Hub is designed to reduce guesswork by grounding answers in your actual source files and documentation with inspectable citations so your engineers can check every answer directly.

faqs.q: What engines are supported right now?
faqs.a: Our current pilot scope—in testing on FDS's own projects—focuses on Roblox Studio (Luau projects and documentation) and Unreal Engine (C++ codebases and technical documentation), with scoped engine reference packs in development. If your team uses another engine, mention it when booking a pilot call and we will give you a straightforward answer on feasibility.
